Pick one (DigitalOcean droplet, Hetzner, Fly.io equivalent, etc.), provision early, and prove a deploy works before the end. title: Pick first model/OCR provider implementation
description: ARCHITECTURE.md isolates the provider behind analyzeLabel/verifyLabel. First concrete impl is undecided. Candidates: Anthropic vision (note F-042 supply-chain risk), OpenAI vision, local Tesseract+small LLM, hosted OCR + LLM split. Decide based on: TTB network restrictions (F-025), 5-second perceived-latency target, prototype budget. Document choice in ARCHITECTURE.md and add provider impl behind the interface.
notes: Decision: Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (released 2026-02-19), via the Gemini API directly. Rationale recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md > Model Provider Boundary. Anthropic excluded on procurement grounds (F-042). xAI excluded — grok-vision still beta. OpenAI GPT-5.5 viable fallback but ~17% behind on MMMU-Pro and 2.5x more expensive. Provider interface narrowed: analyzeLabel on provider, verifyLabel is domain logic (core/verification.ts) operating on ExtractedFields. Verification is two-layer per F-045/REQ-011: Layer 1 well-formedness (deterministic), Layer 2 comparison (hybrid: deterministic for warning/ABV/contents, LLM-assisted via the same Gemini provider for brand/class). Production swap path: Vertex AI Government / Azure OpenAI / Bedrock per TTB procurement catalog.

title: Pick SQL access library: Knex vs Kysely
description: ARCHITECTURE.md currently picks Knex; Chair is leaning toward Kysely. Tower writes a short comparison covering: type-safety with TS-strict (Kysely's strength), migration ergonomics (Knex's strength, mature CLI), reviewer familiarity (Knex more conventional, Kysely growing), ecosystem maturity, exit cost if we change later. Output: a 1-paragraph decision recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md and a rewrite of the existing Knex mentions in 'Chosen Stack', 'Why This Stack', and 'Database Responsibilities' sections. Blocks cc-scz so scaffolding doesn't bake in the wrong choice.
notes: Decision: Kysely. Rationale: schema-first type inference aligns with the project's strict TS rules (no any, no casts, noUncheckedIndexedAccess); the shared Database interface doubles as documentation between API and worker; column typos become compile errors. Migration tooling gap (no Knex-style CLI) is small at our scale — a tsx-driven Migrator script is sufficient for ~4-6 expected migrations. Reviewer surprise minimal in 2026. ARCHITECTURE.md updated; cc-scz design notes updated to install kysely + pg + tsx.

title: Author Cockburn-style use cases
description: Critical path: write UC-001 (Verify an alcohol label application) in design/use-cases.yaml so architecture and the prototype scope can be checked against an actor-and-goal-level description. cc-xog has shipped a working stub of the system without a use case ever being written; re-grounding the design via UC-001 is the first action in the May 1 replan. Cockburn-style: ONE main use case with rich extensions, NOT a scattershot of UC-001/UC-002/UC-003. Source material is the existing facts and requirements; do NOT look at src/ or the running app while drafting (that anchors the use case on the implementation rather than on the agent's goal).
design:
FRESH TOWER: read CLAUDE.md, prompts/tower.md, CONTEXT.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, then discovery/sources/S-001..S-005, discovery/facts.yaml, design/requirements.yaml, docs/handoff.md. Do NOT open src/, the running UI, or browse the deployed URL — those anchor the use case on the implementation instead of the agent's goal.

OUTPUT: create design/use-cases.yaml (file does not yet exist). Schema:

use_cases:
  - id: UC-001
    title: 'Verify an alcohol label application'
    primary_actor: 'TTB compliance agent'
    scope: 'colacop prototype'
    level: 'user goal'    # Cockburn level
    preconditions:
      - '...'
    success_guarantee:
      - '...'
    main_success_scenario:
      - step: 1
        actor_action: '...'
        system_response: '...'
    extensions:
      - id: 'UC-001.3a'   # extends step 3 of main scenario
        condition: '...'
        steps:
          - '...'
    supports_requirements:
      - REQ-001
    references_facts:
      - F-004
    out_of_scope:
      - '...'
    open_questions:
      - '...'

EXTENSIONS TO COVER (per docs/handoff.md, expand or merge as needed): submitted file already processed; submitted file still queued or processing; batch of files arrives; extracted field clearly matches application data; extracted field clearly mismatches application data; brand differs only by case/punctuation and needs tolerant matching; government warning text/capitalization fails strict matching; label image is unreadable or low confidence; model provider is unavailable or blocked; application data arrives without label; label arrives without application data.

LEVEL DISCIPLINE: stay at user-goal level. Refer to 'the system' not 'the watcher', 'the queue' not 'data/incoming/', 'the verification result' not 'Layer 1 / Layer 2 / lifecycle / verdict'. Architecture-shaped detail (lifecycle states, verdict enums, watcher mechanics, Kysely schema) belongs in ARCHITECTURE.md and stays there. The use case is an agent's narrative, not a sequence diagram.

CITATIONS: every extension must cite at least one supporting fact (F-XXX) and at least one supported requirement (REQ-XXX). If you find an extension that lacks fact backing, flag it in open_questions — do not invent fact provenance.

FOLLOW-UP: a separate bead covers the WILL/WON'T/MAYBE scope pass and the structured audit. Do not try to do those here — UC-001 first, full-scope (canonical product), then the next session decides what's in for May 1 submission.
acceptance_criteria: 1. design/use-cases.yaml exists and parses as YAML. 2. UC-001 is present with all Cockburn fields (id, title, primary_actor, scope, level, preconditions, success_guarantee, main_success_scenario, extensions, supports_requirements, references_facts, out_of_scope, open_questions). 3. Main success scenario is 6-12 numbered steps with actor_action + system_response per step. 4. Extensions cover the 11 listed cases (or merge them with explicit rationale). 5. Each extension cites at least one F-XXX fact and one REQ-XXX requirement. 6. No reference to lifecycle enum values, verdict enum values, watcher specifics, Kysely, React, Express, or any other implementation detail. 7. Ruby validation passes: ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file("design/use-cases.yaml"); puts "YAML OK"'. 8. Cross-ref check: all F-XXX in references_facts exist in discovery/facts.yaml; all REQ-XXX in supports_requirements exist in design/requirements.yaml.

title: Scope + audit pass: WILL/WON'T/MAYBE for May submission, gap beads from xog audit
description: After UC-001 lands in design/use-cases.yaml, do the scope pass and the structured audit in one Tower session. Output: notes/scope-may-2026.md with WILL/WON'T/MAYBE annotations on each UC-001 step + extension; notes/audit-2026-05-01.md with the per-criterion pass/partial/fail/unverified table for cc-xog acceptance criteria 1-8 plus a use-case-alignment column for each WILL step; and a batch of new beads for each WILL gap (P0) and SHOULD gap (P1).
design:
INPUTS: design/use-cases.yaml (UC-001 from cc-fk3), discovery/facts.yaml, design/requirements.yaml, ARCHITECTURE.md, the running prototype (now allowed — this session's job IS to compare spec vs implementation), notes/sprint-order.md WILL/WON'T/MAYBE strawman.

OUTPUTS:
- notes/scope-may-2026.md: each UC-001 main step + extension marked WILL / WON'T / MAYBE for the Monday submission, with a one-line rationale per non-trivial call.
- notes/audit-2026-05-01.md: a table walking the 8 cc-xog acceptance criteria with columns 'pass / partial / fail / unverified', a 'notes' column, and a separate table walking each WILL step from UC-001 with columns 'covered by built code? y/n/partial', 'evidence', 'gap'.
- new beads for each WILL gap (P0) and each SHOULD gap (P1). MAYBE gaps that didn't make scope: P3 with rationale.

PROCESS:
1. Read UC-001 first. Ground in the actor's goal.
2. Mark scope on each step/extension. Use the strawman in notes/sprint-order.md as a starting point but treat it as inputs to be reviewed, not committed.
3. Run the functional audit — drop fixtures into data/incoming/, walk the UI, exercise each cc-xog acceptance criterion. Record outcomes in the audit doc.
4. Run the use-case audit — for each WILL step, can the agent actually accomplish it through the built code? Record gaps.
5. File gap beads. Use cc- prefix; one bead per discrete fixable thing. No omnibus 'fix everything' beads.

DO NOT in this session: implement fixes, write fixtures, wire up Gemini. Gap beads go on the queue; execution happens in subsequent Trench sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1. notes/scope-may-2026.md exists with WILL/WON'T/MAYBE marked on every UC-001 step and extension, each with a one-line rationale. 2. notes/audit-2026-05-01.md exists with two tables: 8-row functional table covering cc-xog acceptance criteria, N-row use-case table covering UC-001 WILL steps. 3. Every WILL gap from the audit has a corresponding new P0 bead with description + design + acceptance fields filled in. 4. Every SHOULD gap has a corresponding new P1 bead. 5. Each new bead links back to the audit document and the relevant UC-001 step/extension. 6. cc-xog status: closed if all 8 acceptance criteria are at least partial-pass with the partials beaded; left in_progress if any criterion is fail-with-no-bead-filed.

title: Add extraction_confidence (low/med/hi) to Layer 1 result schema
description: Before cc-xog lands the vertical slice, define an extraction_confidence enum (low | med | hi) on the Layer 1 per-field result so the UI can distinguish 'the label says X and X is wrong' from 'we think the label says X but the image was hard to read.' This is per-field extraction confidence, not a verdict-level score — verdicts remain pass / fail / needs_review per REQ-006. Source: F-039 (bad angles, glare, lighting) makes low-confidence reads a real category we have to surface; without an explicit field, REQ-009 (handle imperfect images gracefully) has nothing to hang on. Mapping rule: derive from whatever Gemini 3.1 Pro returns for per-field extraction (logprob band or self-rated score) into three buckets; record the raw value alongside the bucket for future tuning. UI hint: render as a small badge on the field row, not a numeric column. Acceptance: (1) layer1_results table has extraction_confidence column per field result, (2) stub provider returns plausible buckets on fixtures, (3) UI shows a 'low-confidence read' indicator when bucket=low, (4) needs_review verdict still drives the queue, not the confidence bucket alone.

title: Vertical slice: ingestion + worker + stub verifier + review UI
description: First end-to-end pass: Express server, Chokidar watcher (subscribed to .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp AND .json with awaitWriteFinish enabled), worker entry point, Kysely migrations for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results tables, a stubbed analyzeLabel provider returning fixed ExtractedFields, a regulation-aware verifyLabel (in core/verification.ts) implementing the actual TTB rules from F-047/F-048/F-052 against the stubbed extracted fields (no real model call yet), and a queue-first React+Vite review UI. The watcher pairs files by filename stem per F-046/REQ-012: upsert job by stem; image-first creates job, runs Layer 1, then transitions to lifecycle awaiting_application until JSON arrives, at which point Layer 2 runs without re-running Layer 1; json-first creates job in lifecycle awaiting_label with no layer runs; later arrival of the missing sibling drives the appropriate transitions. Browser upload writes through to data/incoming/ so the upload route and the watcher share one ingestion code path. Goal: a label dropped in data/incoming/ ends up reviewable in the UI within seconds. Deps: cc-scz scaffolding task (closed).
design:
STATE MODEL (split axes per Chair decision 2026-04-29). Lifecycle (single column on jobs): awaiting_label | awaiting_application | queued | processing | processed | failed. Verdict (per-field on result rows): Layer 1 fields take pass | fail | needs_review; Layer 2 fields take pass | fail | needs_review | needs_application_data. failed is reserved for system-level failures (worker crash, file-read error); a label whose Layer 1 fields all came back needs_review is processed with bad verdicts, not failed. The verdict-derived 'needs review' UI bucket is a filter over processed jobs whose result rows contain any needs_review.

LAYER 1 SCHEMA (per F-056/REQ-009): each layer1 per-field result row carries an extraction_confidence column with values low | med | hi, derived from whatever signal the extraction model returns (logprobs or self-rated score), bucketized. Store the raw value alongside the bucket for future tuning. The UI renders extraction_confidence as a per-field badge, not a column or numeric score, and never as part of the verdict surface.

CONSUMES: cc-scz scaffolding (package.json, tsconfig, Kysely + pg, docker-compose, data/ dirs). PRODUCES: working ingestion -> Layer 1/2 verifier -> review UI.

KEY FILES (planning, may shift): src/server/index.ts, src/server/routes/jobs.ts (list, get), src/server/routes/upload.ts (multipart label+json; writes through to data/incoming/, never DB-direct), src/worker/index.ts, src/worker/watcher.ts (chokidar subscribed to image+json globs, awaitWriteFinish on, upsert-by-stem), src/worker/pair.ts (stem matching, sibling lookup, lifecycle transitions), src/core/providers/types.ts (LabelProvider interface with analyzeLabel), src/core/providers/stub.ts (stub returning fixed ExtractedFields with plausible per-field extraction_confidence), src/core/verification.ts (verifyLabel({extracted, application}) returning {layer1, layer2}; Layer 1 implements F-047 warning exact-text, F-048 GOVERNMENT WARNING caps+bold check on extracted text, F-052 wine ABV format/tolerance rule; Layer 2 implements F-051/F-053/F-054 mandatory-field comparison plus brand-name tolerant matching per F-030), src/core/schemas.ts (Zod for ApplicationData + provider boundary), src/db/schema.ts (Kysely Database interface for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results), src/db/migrations/001_init.ts, src/web/* (Vite React SPA: queue list view filtered by lifecycle and verdict-rollup, single job detail showing Layer 1 and Layer 2 results separately with extraction_confidence badges per Layer 1 field).

ApplicationData schema per F-046: brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin?. Government warning is NOT in ApplicationData (regulation-defined; see F-046 and F-047).

STUB BOUNDARY: analyzeLabel (the model boundary) is stubbed and returns canned ExtractedFields with plausible extraction_confidence buckets. verifyLabel (the regulatory logic) is REAL — it actually compares the canned extracted fields to the regulation (F-047/F-048/F-052) and to ApplicationData (F-051/F-053/F-054), and produces honest per-field verdicts. This means cc-htd fixtures will produce real verdicts as soon as they exist.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS SLICE (per F-057, REQ-012 out_of_scope_facts): same-stem replacement of an already-ingested file. Dropping a new file with the same stem after a layer has run does not re-version inputs or re-run affected layers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Drop a paired image+JSON into data/incoming/ -> a job appears in the UI within seconds with Layer 1 and Layer 2 per-field results populated; lifecycle transitions queued -> processing -> processed.
2. Drop only an image -> job appears with Layer 1 per-field results (each carrying an extraction_confidence badge) and Layer 2 fields all marked needs_application_data; lifecycle transitions queued -> processing -> awaiting_application.
3. Drop only a JSON -> job appears in lifecycle awaiting_label with no Layer results.
4. Drop the missing sibling later -> existing job is updated (no duplicate created); in the image-first case, lifecycle transitions awaiting_application -> queued -> processing -> processed and Layer 2 re-runs without re-running Layer 1; in the JSON-first case, lifecycle transitions awaiting_label -> queued -> processing -> processed and both layers run.
5. Browser upload of a paired or label-only submission writes the files to data/incoming/ and produces the same internal representation as a watched-directory drop (the watcher is the single ingestion code path).
6. UI distinguishes Layer 1 (well-formedness) vs Layer 2 (comparison) results visually, and renders extraction_confidence as a per-field badge on Layer 1 fields (not a column or numeric score).
7. npm run typecheck, lint, test all pass on the resulting code; pair.ts has unit tests covering all three arrival cases plus the lifecycle transitions in (1)-(4).
8. No real Gemini call yet — analyzeLabel is stubbed. verifyLabel implements real TTB rules (F-047/F-048/F-052/F-051/F-053/F-054) against the stubbed extracted fields, so the prototype produces honest per-field verdicts even before the model boundary is wired up.
